moat_against: Returns are capped at regulator-allowed ROEs — no pricing power; Ohio's ESP V order already cost earnings and Ohio regulatory risk has a scandal history (HB6)
Heavy leverage: long-term debt $26,390M (FY2025 10-K) against equity of $12,510M (financials_history.csv) — funding costs and rate sensitivity are structural
Growth is bought with dilutive capital: the 30% FET stake sale to Brookfield (closed March 2024) diluted transmission earnings to fund the plan
Storm costs and recovery lag are recurring earnings hits across a six-state footprint
moat_for: Regulated franchise monopolies: ten electric utilities serving 6M+ customers in OH, PA, WV, MD, NJ and NY — captive, essential-service demand
Visible rate-base growth: Energize365 plans $36B of investment 2026-2030 (~$6B in 2026), supporting ~10% annual rate-base growth
Formula-rate transmission investment (FERC-regulated, ~50% of 2025 investment) recovers capital faster than traditional rate cases
Constructive recent regulatory outcomes: base rate cases settled/filed across PA, NJ, WV and MD, Ohio base rate case resolved Nov 2025, S&P upgrade to BBB
moat_justification: Regulated franchise monopolies — ten electric utilities serving more than six million customers across Ohio, Pennsylvania, West Virginia, Maryland, New Jersey and New York, plus one of the largest US transmission systems (over 24,000 miles of lines) — give durable, regulator-granted exclusivity and a visible rate-base growth runway (Energize365: $36B of capital investment planned 2026-2030, ~10% annual rate-base growth and 9.8% consolidated ROE cited in Q1 2026 reporting). Capped at 5 because earned returns are set by regulators at allowed ROEs with no pricing power beyond rate cases, the Ohio regulatory history includes the HB6 scandal and ESP V order drag, and the growth plan is funded with heavy leverage (long-term debt $26,390M per the FY2025 10-K contractual-obligations table) while shareholders were diluted by the 30% FET stake sale to Brookfield in March 2024.
name: FirstEnergy Corp.
one_liner: Durable six-state regulated monopoly, moat 5/10, but conservative owner's earnings are negative on every base (normalized -$2.05/share, TTM -$3.08/share) because capex ($4,705M in FY2025) runs well ahead of operating cash flow ($3,700M) — Tier F on this screen; ~10% guided rate-base growth does not clear 15% and no hurdle-clearing price is computable on a negative OE base.

sbc_override.ack_reason: Out-of-band by construction: the band anchors on the last value filed under an engine-read SBC tag, which is $0 for FY2020 under AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense, so any real current figure flags out-of-band. The value is not an estimate — it is the filer's own FY2024 expensed stock-based compensation from Note 5 of its FY2025 10-K, and the median of its three filed gap-year figures (see source).
sbc_override.reason: DATA_GAP:sbc — SBC missing for fiscal years 2023, 2024, 2025 of the last 3 under the engine's tags. The expensed (net-of-capitalized) figure is the correct OE deduction: the capitalized portion is already inside capex, so subtracting the $83-86M total would double-count it. The engine applies a single override value to every missing period; $43M is the median of the three filed expensed figures ($44M / $43M / $39M) and is exactly the FY2024 figure — and FY2024 is the median year of the 3-yr normalized base, so the base is built from the filed figure with at most $5M of error in the non-median years, immaterial against OCF of $1.4-3.7B and a deeply negative OE base either way.
sbc_override.source: Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-18, accession 0001031296-26-000046), Note 5 — Stock-Based Compensation Plans (p.117), table 'Components of Stock-based Compensation Plan Costs': stock-based compensation costs, net of amounts capitalized, were $39M for FY2025, $43M for FY2024 and $44M for FY2023 (total costs $85M / $86M / $83M in the same table). EDGAR companyfacts carries the same series under SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardCompensationCost1 (total) and the capitalized-amount tag, neither of which the engine reads; the engine's own SBC tags (ShareBasedCompensation / AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense) have no annual values after FY2020.
